proof_attempt_summary: Derived a complete informal public-release minimax rate with an explicit integer calendar and a converse covering arbitrary causal allocations, preserving the fixed-table raw-HT comparator. Corrected the fixed-inflation overclaim to finite certificates restricted to eta >= 6×10^18; ordinary factor-two sufficient budgets, sharp constants and exact optimal calendars remain open. D0.5 mathematics and cited sources passed, but the authoritative typed verdict was incremental below field (6.4 < 7.4), not salvageable in scope; the related-work decision finding remains unrepaired, and no F/Lean stage ran.
tldr: On fixed chronological tables with armwise squared-outcome deficits bounded by \(q\) in every prefix, the minimax raw Horvitz--Thompson excess variance, multiplied by \(T^2\), has uniform order \(\min\{Tq^2,q\log(1+Tq)+qT/(K+1)\}\). A public quadratic integer calendar and explicit original-propensity allocation attain it; the converse covers every public deterministic calendar and measurable available-record policy. When \(Tq\to\infty\), the threshold for immediate precision in rate order is \(K+1=\Omega(T/\log(1+Tq))\); bounded \(Tq\) needs no releases in rate order. The separate literal fixed-inflation sandwich is proved only for \(\eta\ge6\cdot10^{18}\), not every prescribed \(\eta>1\).
gap: Available iid batch upper bounds and release-unrestricted lower bounds do not determine the precision price of every public deterministic release calendar on the complete chronological prefix class.
fill: The design problem jointly chooses an integer public release calendar and an available-record allocation rule. Its certificate must match the attainable overhead against every competing calendar and causal policy, with the empirical constant-design oracle unchanged.
